role: Skeptical modeling lead; read-only hypothesis grooming, no new experiments
diagnosis: 38 fits in state do not represent 38 independent hypotheses. Many optimize the same early-April trained candidate ranking representation on reused windows.

v3 is trained with 35-day history and Apr13-May18 labels, then applied to140-day history and84-day forecast. History normalization alone and a different objective do not remove temporal and horizon mismatch.

Prior multiwindow rejection used all80 binary HGB with19features and5week labels, not current top5 LambdaRank24. Its result is evidence against that implementation, not a general theorem against newer training data.
Later snapshot filtering removed1724/4813 user groups (35.8%) versus455/4721 (9.6%) early. Blindly pooling retained rows changes the user distribution and calibration.
Weekly candidate expansion raised top5 oracle .7471->.7813 and .7206->.7533 but actual refit deteriorated; retrieving more positives alone does not teach the ranker to recognize them.

Base retrieved-seen hindsight oracle is .6729/.6512 versus actual .4074/.3619. A large ranking problem remains even before unseen-program discovery; these are hindsight diagnostic bounds, not attainable promises.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Train current preference model on temporally relevant, horizon-matched examples
ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: Preference top-five over12weeks differs from a5week binary target. More recent snapshots expose seasonal schedule and user changes, while explicit history/forecast length and per-opportunity rates distinguish counts produced by different exposure horizons.
ranked_hypotheses.why_prior_failures_not_decisive: Prior recent/pooled models had different labels, loss, feature set and sampling. Normalization experiments reused a frozen function; they did not retrain a target-matched temporal learner.
ranked_hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: Two fixed top5 LambdaRank24 fits: recent-only and pooled early+recent, with equal total weight per snapshot and per retained user. Build all snapshots with exactly35days preceding history and35day label horizons: featurecutoffs Apr13, May18, Jun22; outcomes end May18, Jun22, Jul27 respectively. Early v3 is already trained on35day history/35day outcomes and supplies the frozen baseline evaluated on the SAME rolling35day June22 features/candidates. Fit recent May18-Jun22 and pooled early+recent; evaluate only Jun22-Jul27. Preserve and report original v3 full-history score separately, not as the matched comparator. This isolates temporal training from cumulative-history and horizon differences. Do not score main May18-Jul27, which overlaps new fitting labels.
ranked_hypotheses.next_if_supported: Build limited rolling snapshots with8-12week preference-label horizons plus explicit forecast opportunity normalization. Keep all training labels before each test cutoff. For a full12week backtest May4-Jul27, every fitted model's labels must end byMay4; current v3 labels endMay18 and cannot serve as a leakage-free baseline there. Retrain an appropriate early baseline for that comparison.
ranked_hypotheses.budget: Two fixed fits, roughly15-25min/1-2GB/1CPU including rolling35day feature rebuild. Follow-up8-12week horizon stage separate approval, at most4fits rather than open grid.
risks: Later holdout already explored, not pristine confirmation
Only20weeks available, so long forecast labels leave limited training history
No-positive query filtering changes population across windows
Do not evaluate after final refit on any labels used in that refit
ranked_hypotheses.uncertainty: Strongest untested training-design mismatch, but older recent-only failures reduce confidence. No basis to promise a large score jump.
ranked_hypotheses.block_weighting: Retained candidate rows within each user receive inverse group-size weight; normalize so each snapshot has equal total training weight. Treat each (user, cutoff) as separate contiguous ranking query; labels from disjoint35day blocks avoid repeated overlapping future outcomes. Report excluded no-positive groups per snapshot.
ranked_hypotheses.controlled_attribution: Score frozen earlyv3 and newer models on identical rolling35day heldout features/candidates. Separately score frozen earlyv3 on original105day history; that contrast isolates history-window effects and must not be credited to retraining.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Predict qualifying programme completions at the airing level
ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: Estimate probability that a viewer is on the channel at an airing and stays for >80% uninterrupted, then sum expected qualifying airings per programme across the forecast. This directly targets repeat counts rather than using aggregate expected minutes as a feature.
ranked_hypotheses.why_prior_failures_not_decisive: Weekly features multiply aggregate historical slot intensity by schedule duration; capping source sessions at1hour and marginalizing across slots loses session-start, residual-duration, continuity and programme-length information. Generic item-rank trees cannot reconstruct that missing event information.
ranked_hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: First perform a small descriptive historical calibration: observed completion rate versus programme duration and session residual lifetime by channel/time. Compare the aggregate expected-count ordering with current weekly-minute ordering on an early development window before fitting any large model. Then one regularized airing-probability/count model with fixed shrinkage; evaluate unchanged full target/cold policy.
ranked_hypotheses.budget: Raw streaming/rejoin20-40min/1-2GB; one model or smoothed empirical hazard fit5-15min. No deep sequence model/GPU required. Request approval before event rebuild or fit.
risks: Must model one uninterrupted source session, not sum separately watched fragments
Without channel-switch/source-session identity cached overlaps are insufficient
Treat absent logs as nonwatch only under explicit coverage assumptions
Historical airtime durations allowed; future inputs limited to availability/channel/time
80% rule is participant evidence, not confirmed official formula
ranked_hypotheses.uncertainty: Mechanistically different and potentially useful for long forecast counts; data logging ambiguity can dominate and nullify gains.
ranked_hypotheses.conditional_gate: Evaluate airing-derived counts/completion signal on existing candidate pairs, separately seen and user-new/global-known. Require conditional ranking/calibration improvement before broad retrieval expansion. Validation colleague reports in-shortlist ranking gaps .340/.359 versus retrieval gaps .234/.249; these diagnostics motivate this ordering, not attainable gains.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Separate repeat preference from new-program discovery with historically estimated identities
ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: Use a repeat expert for items already watched and a discovery expert for new-to-history items, with a user-level gate learned only from earlier snapshots. Include shrinkage-based historical item/category/channel effects and broad co-view retrieval so scarce discovery positives are not overwhelmed by repeated-news examples.
ranked_hypotheses.why_prior_failures_not_decisive: Current19/24features are generic numerical counts/context; no explicit item/category identity effect or separate repeat/new calibration. Prior collaborative candidate expansion fed one generic all80 model; it did not train two distinct conditional tasks. Objective-diversity fusion also preserves one shared hypothesis class.
ranked_hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: No-fit diagnostic first: quantify v3 residuals and calibration separately for seen/new and historical categories, with enough support per segment. If no systematic segment errors, do not build experts. If present, two small regularized experts and one prespecified historical gate, selected on earlier temporal data only.
ranked_hypotheses.budget: Diagnostic5min/under1GB. Conditional follow-up2expert fits20-30min/2GB/1CPU; no enormous embedding or sequence-model search.
risks: Target encoding must be temporal/out-of-fold, never calculated from the row's future label
New items require metadata available at feature cutoff or explicit unknown handling
Gate cannot use observed future seen/new fraction
Training fallback/candidates must remain documented and identical in comparison
Sparse new-item positives and household mixtures may prevent reliable estimation
ranked_hypotheses.uncertainty: Lower confidence than temporal redesign; hypothesis is structural error heterogeneity, not a claim that more features will help.

decision_rules.meaningful_gain: Prespecify approximately +0.01 absolute preference MAP as a practical development hurdle, with paired-user uncertainty and no material regression on comparable robustness window. This is an experiment acceptance threshold, not a forecast or guarantee.
decision_rules.avoid: No more unrestricted tiny feature or loss grids, no metric-definition switching to manufacture improvement, no use of remaining Kaggle submission merely to probe a weak local idea.
decision_rules.score_target: 0.8 feasibility is unknown. Local candidate oracles do not bound the unknown official target, and achieved maxima of searched configurations are not global optima.
decision_rules.final_fit: Once a design is selected, supervised final training may use all fully observed pre-Jul27 outcomes in chronologically formed examples. Keep pre-final evaluation evidence separate; future Jul27-Oct19 views remain forbidden.
decision_rules.long_horizon_feasibility: Twenty observed weeks cannot contain both a12week fitting-label block and a later12week holdout. Matched35/35 is a cheap diagnostic, not a claimed test of84day forecasting. A12week backtest necessarily sacrifices training history/outcomes; report this trade-off explicitly.
decision_rules.one_complex_primary: After prespecified cheap diagnostics, choose at most one substantial strategy (airing-level completion/count forecast or conditional learned representation). Do not launch both large searches. Matched35/35 twofit gate is intended to reject explanations cheaply, not marketed as the substantial final gain.

peer_debate.model_research: Initially agreed horizon/airing/gated directions, then prioritized learned WARP-LightFM latent-score and identity-bias features after root verified historical winning method. I agree standalone ALS/cosine failure does not reject conditional learned representation, but retain temporal controlled test as first choice because it isolates a measured mismatch without dependency risk. This priority disagreement remains explicit.
peer_debate.validation: Warns12week May4-Jul27 evaluation overlaps v3 training throughMay18; baseline must be refit with outcomes endingMay4. Flags no-positive sampling shift and uninterrupted-session/negative-label semantics. Both objections incorporated. Further decomposition indicates approximately half remaining top5 AP mass is seen-item ranking and half user-new/global-known, with globally new items minor. Require conditional signal on existing pairs before expansion; incorporated into airing-model gate.

additional_competing_hypothesis.name: Bounded learned WARP latent features
additional_competing_hypothesis.reason: Static cosine/counted associations and standalone ALS do not exhaust learned ranking representations; append latent score/item bias/user bias/norms to fixed v3 pool before expanding retrieval.
additional_competing_hypothesis.cheap_test: One small16factor10epoch WARP model with bounded negatives and one fixed ranker refit; compare conditional gain on same chronological cutoffs. Must approve dependency installation and resource estimate first.
additional_competing_hypothesis.caveat: Participant success is motivation, not evidence our data/proxy/protocol will improve. User bias constant within query needs nonlinear interactions to affect within-user ordering.
